finding.claim: POST /settings/email is decorated with @login_optional instead of @login_required, so unauthenticated requests reach change_email with g.uid = None and call set_email(None, ...).
finding.source: Anonymous HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie (routes.py:34-35; login_optional at routes.py:19-25 sets g.uid = session.get('uid') = None and never aborts).

trace.note: login_optional sets g.uid from session.get('uid') and never aborts.
change_email calls set_email(g.uid, ...) with g.uid possibly None; no None check.
Returns ok=True to the anonymous caller.
set_email is a stub; a real implementation with uid None could match WHERE uid IS NULL or act on an unintended identity.

finding.guards_checked: login_optional (routes.py:19-25): does not enforce auth. No None check on g.uid in change_email (routes.py:36-38). Sibling /settings/password (routes.py:41-42) uses @login_required, which aborts 401 (routes.py:11-12). Impact is conditional on the real set_email implementation, which is not in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. login_optional (routes.py:19-25) sets g.uid = session.get("uid") and never aborts. change_email (routes.py:36-38) has no None check and calls set_email(g.uid, ...) unconditionally. The only auth gate in the file, login_required (routes.py:8-16, abort(401) at line 12), is applied to /settings/password (routes.py:42), not to /settings/email.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: the anonymous POST to /settings/email is decorated with @login_optional at routes.py:35, so change_email runs at routes.py:37 with g.uid possibly None and nothing stops it.
